suggestions.rationale: Deferred from ACDT #100 with explicit 'next call' revisit. Strong community support to include SETCODEFROM, data repricing (EIP-8279), nonce bump (EIP-8253), and deactivate self-destruct. jochem raised that if deactivate self-destruct ships, EIP-8360 (TCREATE) should be prioritized to avoid economic disruption.

suggestions.topic: Hoodi testnet fork status and client readiness
suggestions.rationale: Client releases were due October 16th (yesterday). Go/no-go decision for Hoodi fork (tentatively October 27) was planned for October 8 but not documented. Need confirmation all releases are out and readiness for October 27 activation.
ACDT #100 reported Nimbus, Erigon, Lighthouse, Grandine, and Besu nodes offline on Glamsterdam devnet. Client teams were asked to investigate but no resolution was documented.
bogota-devnet-1 was targeting launch on October 15th (today). heze-devnet-2 targeting October 28th latest (3+ CL clients required). Need status updates on both launches and any blockers encountered.

suggestions.topic: EIP-7870 hardware specs update for Glamsterdam
suggestions.rationale: ACDT #100 confirmed current 500 MB/s sequential read/write specs are too low for Glamsterdam; jochem recommends 2000 MB/s. Barnabas noted random 4K IOPS matter more than sequential MB/s. Decision made to keep EIP-7870 as living document with fork-specific updates, but actual spec update not yet completed.

suggestions.topic: Repricing decision following devnet-8 and mainnet shadow fork retests
suggestions.rationale: ACDT #98 deferred repricing pending retests without debug tracing on devnet-8 and mainnet shadow fork (~1.5-2 weeks from Sept 28 = mid-October). ACDT #99 shadow fork round 2 went smoothly, but explicit repricing decision not yet documented. jochemnet shadow fork v2 with 64KB contracts launched post-Sepolia fork for benchmarking.

suggestions.topic: CL serving window and BAL retention alignment
suggestions.rationale: Deferred from ACDT #97 to be brought to ACDE before next call. No subsequent ACDT meetings reference this discussion. While deferred, the 'before next call' target has passed without documented resolution, suggesting this may have been handled async or deprioritized.

suggestions.topic: Fast Confirmation Rule 'confirmed' block tag implementation approach
suggestions.rationale: ACDT #98 decided FCR should be opt-in via compatible CL+EL pairs without requiring hard fork, with implementation approach to be investigated. Julian Ma was to open async thread (execution-apis #908). Chainlink went live with FCR; other bridges and L2s blocked by RPC providers needing to serve both safe and FCR simultaneously.
